---
title: "Diet indices vs beta diversity"
author: "Giacomo Antonello"
format: html
params:
  distance: "Bray-Curtis"
  outdir: "results/beta_diversity"
  n_permutations: 999
  n_permutations_covariates: 999
  n_cores: 4
---

**Questions**, for one beta diversity distance (`distance` parameter) and each diet index:

  1. **PERMANOVA**: does community composition change with the diet index,
     after adjusting for covariates? `distance ~ diet index + Condition(covariates)`.
     Also, how much of the variation does each covariate explain?
  2. **Betadisper**: does the within-group variability (dispersion) differ
     across quartiles of the diet index?
  3. **PCoA**: how do samples spread along the main axes of variation, colored
     by diet index?
  4. **Distance-based RDA (dbRDA)**: which part of community composition follows
     the diet index, after removing the covariates?

Each render analyzes one distance, so the distances can run as separate jobs at
the same time (see `run-beta-distance.sh` and `Analyses/README.md`).
`05-beta-summary.qmd` then combines the distances and computes the FDR across them.

# Distances

| Distance (`distance` parameter) | Feature table | Source |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| `Bray-Curtis` | genus relative abundance | computed here |
| `Canberra` | genus relative abundance | computed here |
| `unweighted_UniFrac` | ASVs (DADA2 RB) rarefied to 10,000 reads | pre-calculated by NHANES |
| `weighted_UniFrac` | ASVs (DADA2 RB) rarefied to 10,000 reads | pre-calculated by NHANES |

UniFrac needs a phylogenetic tree, which is not in the public release, so the
NHANES matrices are used. Bray-Curtis and Canberra are computed from the same
genus counts used for the Dirichlet Multinomial Mixtures, with the same
prevalence filter (at least 10 counts in at least 50 samples). Canberra weighs
every genus equally regardless of abundance, so it is the distance most
sensitive to rare genera; Bray-Curtis is dominated by abundant genera.

# Survey design

Models are unweighted: PERMANOVA and betadisper have no standard survey-weighted
versions (see the Survey weighting section of `03-diet-vs-alpha.qmd`).
Instead, permutations are restricted within NHANES strata (`SDMVSTRA`), and the
covariates include the variables used for oversampling (age, race/ethnicity, income).

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(mia)
library(vegan)
library(data.table)
library(patchwork)
library(openxlsx2)

seed <- 1234
set.seed(seed)
theme_set(theme_light(base_size = 14))

load("../NHANES_oral_microbiome.se.rda")
```

# Variables

Edit the vectors below to change the analysis. To drop a covariate, delete
(or comment out) its line in `covariates`; everything downstream adapts.

```{r variables}
# exposures. TODO: add MaPiDS when available
diet_indices <- c(
  "HEI-2020" = "HEI2020_ALL",
  "UPF (% calories)" = "nova4_propcal",
  "UPF (% grams)" = "nova4_propg"
)

# adjustment set
covariates <- c(
  "age",                # years
  "sex",
  "raceth",             # race/ethnicity
  "edu",                # education
  "pir",                # family income to poverty ratio
  "smoke_status",
  "alcohol_cat",
  "bmi",
  "kcal",               # total energy intake
  "OH_n_natural_teeth", # number of natural teeth
  "cycle"               # NHANES cycle, 2009-2010 or 2011-2012
)

# reference levels of categorical covariates
reference_levels <- list(
  sex = "Female",
  raceth = "Non_Hispanic_White",
  edu = "College_or_Above",
  smoke_status = "Never",
  alcohol_cat = "No_12plus_drinks",
  cycle = "2009-2010"
)

# pre-calculated NHANES distance matrices
nhanes_distance_files <- c(
  "unweighted_UniFrac" = "../../microbiome-data/dada2rb-unwunifrac-beta.txt",
  "weighted_UniFrac" = "../../microbiome-data/dada2rb-wunifrac-beta.txt"
)

# distances computed from the genus table
computed_distances <- c("Bray-Curtis" = "bray", "Canberra" = "canberra")

distance <- params$distance
stopifnot(distance %in% c(names(computed_distances), names(nhanes_distance_files)))
distance_label <- str_replace(distance, "_", " ")

# one output folder per number of permutations (for sensitivity analyses) and distance,
# e.g. results/beta_diversity/perm999_covperm999/Bray-Curtis
run_label <- sprintf("perm%d_covperm%d", params$n_permutations, params$n_permutations_covariates)
distance_outdir <- file.path(params$outdir, run_label, distance)
dir.create(distance_outdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Analytic sample

Unlike the alpha diversity models, a single analytic sample is used for all
indices and distances (complete cases for all diet indices and covariates), so
that results are comparable across distances. Diet indices are standardized
(mean 0, SD 1).

```{r analytic sample}
metadata.df <- data.frame(colData(NHANES_oral_microbiome.se))

# character covariates to factors with the chosen reference level
for (covariate in intersect(names(reference_levels), covariates)) {
  metadata.df[[covariate]] <- relevel(factor(metadata.df[[covariate]]), ref = reference_levels[[covariate]])
}

analytic.df <- metadata.df %>%
  # unname, otherwise select() renames the columns to the labels
  select(SEQN, SDMVSTRA, all_of(unname(c(diet_indices, covariates)))) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(
    across(all_of(unname(diet_indices)), \(x) as.numeric(scale(x))),
    SDMVSTRA = factor(SDMVSTRA)
  )

nrow(analytic.df)
```

# Distance matrix

```{r distance, message=FALSE}
# read an NHANES square distance matrix, keeping only the analytic sample in its order
read_nhanes_distance <- function(file, samples) {
  distance.dt <- fread(file, select = c("SEQN", samples), colClasses = c(SEQN = "character"))
  distance.mat <- as.matrix(distance.dt[match(samples, distance.dt$SEQN), -1])
  rownames(distance.mat) <- samples
  as.dist(distance.mat[, samples])
}

if (distance %in% names(computed_distances)) {
  # same prevalence filter as the Dirichlet Multinomial Mixtures
  critical_prev <- 50/ncol(NHANES_oral_microbiome.se)
  genus_relative_abundance <- NHANES_oral_microbiome.se %>%
    subsetByPrevalent(assay.type = "counts", detection = 10, prevalence = critical_prev) %>%
    assay("counts") %>%
    t()
  genus_relative_abundance <- genus_relative_abundance[analytic.df$SEQN, ]
  genus_relative_abundance <- genus_relative_abundance / rowSums(genus_relative_abundance)

  beta_dist <- vegdist(genus_relative_abundance, method = computed_distances[[distance]])
} else {
  beta_dist <- read_nhanes_distance(nhanes_distance_files[[distance]], samples = analytic.df$SEQN)
}

# check that the distance has no missing values for the analytic sample
stopifnot(!anyNA(beta_dist))
```

# PERMANOVA

The PERMANOVA is split in two parts, with different aims and costs.

**Diet indices** (main result). For each diet index, only the diet index is
tested, after adjusting for all covariates: the model is
`distance ~ diet index + Condition(covariates)`, fitted with `vegan::dbrda` and
tested with `anova()`. The covariates are still in the model, so the diet
index is adjusted for them exactly as in a PERMANOVA with the index last. Its
R2 and pseudo-F are the same as the index row of
`adonis2(distance ~ covariates + diet index, by = "margin")`; the permutations
are of the residuals after the covariates (`anova.cca` default, reduced model),
the usual scheme to test one term while adjusting for others.
`n_permutations` permutations; the FDR is computed across distances in
`05-beta-summary.qmd`. To check how p-values depend on the number of
permutations, render again with another `n_permutations`: results of each
number of permutations go to their own folder.

**Covariates** (descriptive). One `adonis2` with all covariates and
`by = "margin"`: each covariate is tested after adjusting for all the others,
so the results do not depend on the order of the formula. The diet index is
left out, because covariate effects barely change across the diet models.
`n_permutations_covariates` permutations: a minimum p-value of 0.001 is enough
to describe the covariates. FDR is within this distance.

Testing every term of every model with `n_permutations` permutations would
take about 9 times longer for the same diet results.

```{r permanova diet indices}
diet_permutations <- how(nperm = params$n_permutations, blocks = analytic.df$SDMVSTRA)

run_diet_permanova <- function(diet) {
  model <- dbrda(
    as.formula(sprintf("beta_dist ~ %s + Condition(%s)", diet, paste(covariates, collapse = " + "))),
    data = analytic.df
  )
  set.seed(seed)
  test <- anova(model, permutations = diet_permutations, parallel = params$n_cores)
  tibble(R2 = model$CCA$tot.chi / model$tot.chi, F = test$F[1], p.value = test$`Pr(>F)`[1])
}

permanova_results.df <- tibble(distance = distance_label, diet_label = names(diet_indices), diet = diet_indices) %>%
  mutate(permanova = map(diet, run_diet_permanova)) %>%
  select(distance, diet_label, permanova) %>%
  unnest(permanova)

knitr::kable(permanova_results.df, digits = 4)
```

```{r permanova covariates}
covariate_permutations <- how(nperm = params$n_permutations_covariates, blocks = analytic.df$SDMVSTRA)

set.seed(seed)
permanova_covariates.df <- adonis2(
  reformulate(covariates, response = "beta_dist"),
  data = analytic.df,
  permutations = covariate_permutations,
  by = "margin",
  parallel = params$n_cores
) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("term")

# covariate rows only, FDR within this distance
permanova_covariates_results.df <- permanova_covariates.df %>%
  filter(term %in% covariates) %>%
  transmute(distance = distance_label, term, Df, R2, F, p.value = `Pr(>F)`) %>%
  mutate(p.adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"))

knitr::kable(permanova_covariates_results.df, digits = 4)
```

# Betadisper

Dispersion is compared across quartiles of each diet index. Betadisper does not
adjust for covariates.

```{r betadisper}
run_betadisper <- function(diet) {
  quartile <- factor(paste0("Q", ntile(analytic.df[[diet]], 4)))
  dispersion <- betadisper(beta_dist, quartile, type = "median")
  set.seed(seed)
  test <- permutest(dispersion, permutations = diet_permutations, parallel = params$n_cores)

  list(
    distance_to_median = tibble(SEQN = analytic.df$SEQN, quartile, distance_to_median = dispersion$distances),
    test = tibble(F = test$tab["Groups", "F"], p.value = test$tab["Groups", "Pr(>F)"])
  )
}

betadisper.df <- tibble(distance = distance_label, diet_label = names(diet_indices), diet = diet_indices) %>%
  mutate(betadisper = map(diet, run_betadisper))

betadisper_results.df <- betadisper.df %>%
  mutate(test = map(betadisper, "test")) %>%
  select(distance, diet_label, test) %>%
  unnest(test)

knitr::kable(betadisper_results.df, digits = 4)
```

```{r betadisper plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
betadisper_distances.df <- betadisper.df %>%
  mutate(data = map(betadisper, "distance_to_median")) %>%
  select(diet_label, data) %>%
  unnest(data)

betadisper_plot <- ggplot(betadisper_distances.df, aes(x = quartile, y = distance_to_median)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ diet_label) +
  labs(
    title = distance_label,
    x = "Diet index quartile",
    y = "Distance to group median"
  )

betadisper_plot
```

# PCoA

```{r pcoa}
pcoa <- cmdscale(beta_dist, k = 2, eig = TRUE)

# share of the positive eigenvalues (non-Euclidean distances have negative ones)
variance_explained <- 100 * pcoa$eig[1:2] / sum(pcoa$eig[pcoa$eig > 0])

pcoa_coordinates.df <- tibble(SEQN = analytic.df$SEQN, PCo1 = pcoa$points[, 1], PCo2 = pcoa$points[, 2])
coordinates.df <- dplyr::left_join(pcoa_coordinates.df, analytic.df, by = "SEQN")

pcoa_plot <- imap(diet_indices, \(diet, diet_label) ggplot(coordinates.df, aes(x = PCo1, y = PCo2, color = .data[[diet]])) +
                    geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
                    scale_color_viridis_c() +
                    labs(
                      x = sprintf("PCo1 (%.1f%%)", variance_explained[1]),
                      y = sprintf("PCo2 (%.1f%%)", variance_explained[2]),
                      color = paste0(diet_label, "\n(SD)")
                    )) %>%
  wrap_plots(nrow = 1) +
  plot_annotation(title = distance_label)
```

```{r pcoa plots, fig.width=15, fig.height=5}
pcoa_plot
```

# Distance-based RDA

PCoA shows the largest axes of variation, which need not be related to diet.
dbRDA (`vegan::capscale`) is a PCoA constrained to the diet index, with the
covariates partialled out (`Condition()`): the constrained axis (CAP1) is the
direction in community space that best follows the diet index after adjusting
for covariates, and MDS1 is the largest remaining (unconstrained) axis. It is the
visual counterpart of the PERMANOVA; the PERMANOVA provides the test.

Negative eigenvalues of non-Euclidean distances (Bray-Curtis, Canberra) are
discarded by `capscale`, so inertia proportions refer to the Euclidean part.

Plotted site scores are weighted-average ("wa") scores, i.e. each sample's
community projected onto the axes. With a single constraint, the alternative
linear-combination ("lc") scores are just the diet index itself. Because wa
scores carry the full community, CAP1 and MDS1 can be correlated in the plot.

```{r dbrda}
run_dbrda <- function(diet) {
  dbrda_formula <- as.formula(sprintf("beta_dist ~ %s + Condition(%s)", diet, paste(covariates, collapse = " + ")))
  capscale(dbrda_formula, data = analytic.df)
}

dbrda.df <- tibble(distance = distance_label, diet_label = names(diet_indices), diet = diet_indices) %>%
  mutate(model = map(diet, run_dbrda))

dbrda_results.df <- dbrda.df %>%
  transmute(
    distance, diet_label,
    total_inertia = map_dbl(model, \(m) m$tot.chi),
    covariates_inertia = map_dbl(model, \(m) m$pCCA$tot.chi),
    diet_inertia = map_dbl(model, \(m) m$CCA$tot.chi),
    # share of all variation, and of the variation left after the covariates
    diet_prop_total = diet_inertia / total_inertia,
    diet_prop_partial = diet_inertia / (total_inertia - covariates_inertia)
  )

knitr::kable(dbrda_results.df, digits = 4)
```

```{r dbrda plots, fig.width=15, fig.height=5}
dbrda_plot <- dbrda.df %>%
  pmap(function(distance, diet_label, diet, model) {
    site_scores <- scores(model, display = "sites", choices = 1:2, scaling = "sites")
    cap_prop <- 100 * model$CCA$tot.chi / (model$tot.chi - model$pCCA$tot.chi)
    mds_prop <- 100 * model$CA$eig[1] / (model$tot.chi - model$pCCA$tot.chi)

    tibble(SEQN = analytic.df$SEQN, CAP1 = site_scores[, 1], MDS1 = site_scores[, 2], index = analytic.df[[diet]]) %>%
      ggplot(aes(x = CAP1, y = MDS1, color = index)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.6) +
      scale_color_viridis_c() +
      labs(
        x = sprintf("CAP1, %s (%.2f%%)", diet_label, cap_prop),
        y = sprintf("MDS1 (%.1f%%)", mds_prop),
        color = paste0(diet_label, "\n(SD)")
      )
  }) %>%
  wrap_plots(nrow = 1) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = distance_label,
    subtitle = "Covariates partialled out; % of variation remaining after covariates"
  )

dbrda_plot
```

# Write results

All results go to the folder of this distance. `05-beta-summary.qmd` reads
them to build the summary across distances.

```{r write results}
write_xlsx(
  list(diet_indices = permanova_results.df, covariates = permanova_covariates.df),
  file = file.path(distance_outdir, "PERMANOVA.xlsx")
)
write_xlsx(
  list(test = betadisper_results.df, distance_to_median = betadisper_distances.df),
  file = file.path(distance_outdir, "betadisper.xlsx")
)
write_xlsx(
  list(
    coordinates = pcoa_coordinates.df,
    eigenvalues = tibble(axis = seq_along(pcoa$eig), eigenvalue = pcoa$eig)
  ),
  file = file.path(distance_outdir, "PCoA.xlsx")
)
write_xlsx(
  list(
    inertia = dbrda_results.df,
    site_scores = dbrda.df %>%
      mutate(scores = map(model, \(m) scores(m, display = "sites", choices = 1:2, scaling = "sites") %>%
                            as_tibble() %>% mutate(SEQN = analytic.df$SEQN, .before = 1))) %>%
      select(diet_label, scores) %>% unnest(scores)
  ),
  file = file.path(distance_outdir, "dbRDA.xlsx")
)
ggsave(plot = betadisper_plot, filename = file.path(distance_outdir, "betadisper_boxplots.svg"), height = 4, width = 10)
ggsave(plot = pcoa_plot, filename = file.path(distance_outdir, "PCoA_by_diet_index.png"), height = 5, width = 15, dpi = 300)
ggsave(plot = dbrda_plot, filename = file.path(distance_outdir, "dbRDA_by_diet_index.png"), height = 5, width = 15, dpi = 300)
```
